scope: Native recovery handback requires its recorded speed-cap lease
finding: DrivingRecoveryRelease could stop/redirect an otherwise exact reverse even when a mission/controller replaced its forced-speed cap; normal assistance checked its cap but cleanup did not. Recovery capture fell back from absent effective commander to driver, while release compared the raw effectiveCommander directly.
change: Native recovery handback and pending retention require current forced-speed value within0.1m/s of the journal cap. Main callback also revokes changed-cap recovery before release/reacquisition, preserving existing route-yield semantics. Release resolves missing effective commander to current driver and still requires original identity. Changed-cap release remains metadata-only and does not restore speed or issue movement.

validation.initial_focused_failure: One whitespace-sensitive locator expected _mayIssueDriving= instead of existing spaced declaration; corrected without changing the guard.

limits: Same-value external cap/command edits remain ambiguous without declared ownership.
No real cap replacement during an observed native reverse, commander transition, HC migration or repeatability acceptance.
Deferred exact handback while the entire subsystem is disabled still lacks demonstrated later observation; this commit does not add an observer or resolve that gap.
No physical recovery success, queue-cascade resolution or performance-budget acceptance. All65 feature families remain partial.
